items.title: There's no scientific evidence tying 5G networks to the coronavirus pandemic. Howe...
items.snippet_en: There is no scientific evidence to support a link between 5G technology and the spread of COVID-19. Conspiracy theories linking 5G to the coronavirus pandemic have circulated online, leading to incidents such as the burning of cell towers in the UK and other European countries. Regulators have set limits on the radiation power of 5G devices.

items.title: No, 5G networks do not cause coronavirus
items.snippet_en: There is no scientific evidence to support a link between 5G technology and the spread of COVID-19. Conspiracy theories linking 5G to the coronavirus pandemic have circulated online, leading to incidents such as the burning of cell towers in the UK and other European countries. These theories often suggest that 5G either causes the virus or weakens the immune system.

The claim that 5G mobile towers spread the coronavirus is false. COVID-19 is a viral disease caused by the SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus, and it spreads through respiratory droplets. Viruses cannot travel on radio waves or mobile networks. COVID-19 has spread in many countries that do not have 5G networks.

items.title: 5G Doesn’t Cause COVID-19, But the Rumor It Does Spreads Like a Virus
items.snippet_en: There is no scientific evidence to support a link between 5G technology and the spread of COVID-19. COVID-19 is a viral disease caused by the SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus. 5G uses non-ionizing radiation, which does not damage DNA or cause cancer.

items.title: Fact Check: 'Completely Bogus' Claim 5G Tech Invites Coronavirus
items.snippet_en: The claim that 5G mobile towers spread the coronavirus is false. There is no scientific evidence to support a link between 5G technology and the spread of COVID-19. Conspiracy theories often suggest that 5G either causes the virus, weakens the immune system, or that Wuhan was the first city to roll out 5G. The World Health Organization (WHO) states there is no connection.

The claim that 5G mobile towers spread the coronavirus is false. There is no scientific evidence to support a link between 5G technology and the spread of COVID-19. Conspiracy theories often suggest that 5G either causes the virus, weakens the immune system, or that Wuhan was the first city to roll out 5G.

outputs.notes_en: All sources contradict the claim that 5G mobile towers spread the coronavirus. They consistently state there is no scientific evidence to support such a link, and explain that COVID-19 is a viral disease spread through respiratory droplets, not radio waves. Several sources also mention the prevalence of conspiracy theories linking 5G to COVID-19.
